name: Loadsmart
desc: Freight technology company offering truckload, intermodal and drayage brokerage plus transportation management and dock scheduling software for shippers.
markets: Mainly US shippers and carriers with cross-border Mexico freight; teams in Brazil and Mexico; reported 2026 Opendock entry into Europe.
rationale: Freight-tech brand selling to large shippers; F1 hospitality could reach enterprise logistics buyers, though marketing is mainly US and B2B.

name: At-Bay
desc: Insurtech providing cyber insurance and technology errors and omissions cover with security scanning, sold to businesses through brokers.
markets: Policies sold to US small and mid-size businesses via brokers; remote hiring in Canada, but no confirmed customers outside the US.
rationale: Cyber insurer with mostly US broker distribution; F1 could showcase security technology, but domestic reach limits value.

name: Macnica Galaxy Inc.
desc: Distributor of semiconductor components and AI hardware, including NVIDIA products, with technical services for server, industrial and automotive customers.
markets: Customers in Taiwan, mainland China and Hong Kong via its GFEi subsidiary, and elsewhere in Asia; no verified wider footprint.
rationale: B2B component distributor within Macnica group; little brand marketing need, though AI hardware partners give some technology angle.
changed: Joined the Macnica group of Japan in 2010

name: Presidio
desc: IT solutions provider delivering networking, cloud, cybersecurity and managed services to enterprise and public-sector customers.
markets: More than 50 US offices plus about nine offices across EMEA and Asia-Pacific, including Ireland, London, Singapore and India.
rationale: Large IT integrator competing with F1-sponsoring Deloitte and Cognizant; B2B hospitality and technology showcase for enterprise clients.

name: Unqork
desc: No-code enterprise application platform used by banks, insurers, healthcare organisations and governments to build business software without hand-written code.
markets: Mainly US financial, insurance and public-sector clients; London office and EMEA sales team serving European customers.
rationale: Enterprise software firm selling to banks and insurers; F1 hospitality and AI technology showcase could support US and EMEA sales.

name: Beyond Identity
desc: Cybersecurity company selling passwordless, phishing-resistant authentication and device trust software to enterprises and technology companies.
markets: Mainly US enterprise customers; directories report European offices and a Frankfurt data centre serving European clients (not confirmed by company).
rationale: Identity-security vendor; rivals Okta and CrowdStrike already sponsor F1, so a technology showcase partnership is plausible.

name: Virtana
desc: Software company providing hybrid and multi-cloud observability, capacity planning and cost optimisation for large enterprises and public-sector organisations.
markets: US enterprises plus an established customer base in EMEA and Asia-Pacific, which it announced plans to expand in October 2025.
rationale: Observability rivals Dynatrace and Splunk sponsor F1; B2B hospitality and data showcase could support EMEA and APAC expansion.
changed: Formerly Virtual Instruments; acquired OpsCruise in 2023

name: LinkSquares
desc: Software company offering an AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform for legal and finance teams at mid-sized and large companies.
markets: More than 1,000 customers, apparently mostly US companies; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Niche legal-tech vendor focused on the US mid-market; weak F1 fit beyond limited B2B hospitality.

name: Panzura
desc: Hybrid-cloud data management company providing a global file system for enterprises sharing unstructured files across multiple locations.
markets: Mainly US enterprises; an older company page cites satellite offices in the UK and New Zealand; current footprint not confirmed.
rationale: Storage rivals NetApp and VAST Data sponsor F1; plausible B2B technology showcase, though scale and marketing budget are modest.
changed: Assets acquired and company re-founded under Profile Capital Management in 2020

name: Alt Inc.
desc: Japanese AI developer known for the AI GIJIROKU meeting transcription service and large language model products for businesses.
markets: Customers in Japan only; company is in court-supervised rehabilitation after an accounting fraud, with no expansion plans.
rationale: Delisted after revenue fraud and in civil rehabilitation; no realistic F1 fit.
changed: Delisted from Tokyo Stock Exchange in August 2025 after revenue fraud; filed for civil rehabilitation in 2025

name: EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure
desc: Developer, owner and operator of wholesale hyperscale data centre campuses leased to large cloud and technology tenants.
markets: Campuses in six North American markets including Northern Virginia, Phoenix, Santa Clara and Reno; plans new regions from 2026.
rationale: Wholesale data-centre landlord with a handful of hyperscale tenants; little need for brand marketing, weak F1 fit.

name: Serverfarm
desc: Data centre developer and operator offering colocation, wholesale and build-to-suit facilities to enterprise and cloud customers.
markets: Data centres in North America, Europe and Israel, including Toronto and Houston; joint venture planned with IPTO in Greece.
rationale: Infrastructure landlord with few large customers; some B2B hospitality value but limited brand need.
changed: Controlling interest acquired by Manulife Investment Management's infrastructure fund (announced 2023)

name: Flo Networks
desc: Fiber network operator providing connectivity, data transport and digital infrastructure services to businesses and carriers across the US and Mexico.
markets: Owns fiber across the southern US and Mexico, with presence in over 40 Mexican cities; tender offers for Axtel announced 2026.
rationale: US-Mexico telecom carrier; Mexico City and US Grands Prix offer B2B hospitality for enterprise and carrier customers.
changed: Renamed from Transtelco in 2022; bought American Tower's Mexico fiber unit in 2023; Axtel tender offers announced 2026, not completed

name: Conclusion
desc: Dutch group of more than 30 IT companies providing software, cloud, data, security and consulting services to businesses and government.
markets: Clients mainly in the Netherlands; no verified operations elsewhere; main sponsor of FC Utrecht football club.
rationale: Already sponsors FC Utrecht, showing sports marketing appetite, but Dutch-focused reach makes global F1 value limited.
changed: Acquired IT service provider Mediaan (date not confirmed)

name: Zetrix AI Berhad
desc: Malaysian group running e-government services and the Zetrix blockchain for digital identity, payments and cross-border trade.
markets: Malaysia and the Philippines government services; cross-border blockchain and digital ID links with China.
rationale: Government-facing digital services group in Asia; limited consumer marketing need, plausible only for Singapore GP hospitality.
changed: MY E.G. Services renamed Zetrix AI Berhad (by 2026)

name: Eclairion
desc: French high-density computing centre hosting high-performance computing and AI clusters in container modules for research and technology clients.
industry: HPC and AI data centre hosting
markets: Operates in France only, hosting Mistral AI's cluster; plans new sites in Sarthe and Moselle.
rationale: Single-country infrastructure operator serving a few AI and research tenants, with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Pivot3
desc: Former maker of hyperconverged storage and computing systems, mainly for video surveillance, sold to enterprises and governments.
markets: No longer operates; its surveillance products are sold by Quantum as the VS-HCI Series.
rationale: Company no longer exists after its assets were sold to Quantum; no F1 fit.
changed: Surveillance portfolio and assets acquired by Quantum Corporation in July 2021; company wound down

name: Quess Corp
desc: Indian staffing and workforce management company providing general and IT staffing to thousands of enterprises across many sectors.
markets: Mainly India, with operations reported in about nine countries across South-East Asia, North America and the Middle East.
rationale: Staffing rivals Randstad and ManpowerGroup sponsor F1; could use F1 for employer branding and B2B hospitality in India and Gulf.
changed: Demerged Digitide Solutions and Bluspring Enterprises as separately listed companies in 2025

name: Victory Capital Holdings
desc: Asset manager owning multiple investment franchises that offer mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts through advisers and institutions.
markets: Mainly US clients; about 17 percent of assets from non-US clients in 60 countries; staff in London, Hong Kong and Singapore.
rationale: Growing asset manager reaching advisers; F1 hospitality could support distribution, though brand is mostly US and B2B.
changed: Agreed in August 2026 to acquire First Eagle Investments, not completed (expected close Q1 2027)

name: Cloud Capital
desc: Investment manager running closed-end funds that acquire, develop and operate data centres for institutional investors.
markets: Investors and data centre assets in the US and abroad; offices reported in Washington, San Francisco and London.
rationale: Specialist fund manager with no consumer or operating brand; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: Propel Finance
desc: Welsh non-bank lender providing asset finance and refinance for equipment and vehicles to UK small and medium businesses.
markets: Lends to UK businesses only, directly and through partners such as Barclays; no verified expansion abroad.
rationale: UK-only SME lender with limited marketing scale and no international customers; weak F1 fit beyond UK hospitality.

name: Aukera
desc: Renewable energy developer building and operating battery storage, solar and wind projects across several European countries.
markets: Projects in the UK, Romania, Belgium, Germany and Italy; about 1 GW built or under construction.
rationale: Project developer selling power to utilities and grids; little brand need, weak F1 fit.

name: Patria Investments
desc: Alternative asset manager offering private equity, infrastructure, credit, real estate and public equity funds to institutional and private investors.
markets: Invests in Latin America, Europe and the US; offices across South America plus New York, London, Dubai and Hong Kong.
rationale: Investor-facing brand with São Paulo base; F1 hospitality in Brazil and Gulf could help fundraising, though plausible rather than obvious.
changed: Completed acquisition of WP Global Partners in April 2026

name: Inseego
desc: Maker of 5G mobile hotspots, fixed wireless access routers and cloud management software sold to carriers and businesses.
markets: Focused on its domestic US 5G business with US carriers after selling its UK, EU and Australian telematics unit in 2024.
rationale: US carrier-channel hardware supplier with modest brand marketing and domestic focus; weak F1 fit.
changed: Sold telematics business to Ctrack Holdings in December 2024
